subject: english
title: Ae：篇章

content.summary: 本課聚焦「篇章」，以自編範例練習概念、證據與新情境遷移。

sections.heading: 學習目標
sections.body: 能根據題目提供的條件、資料或情境，辨識並說明「篇章」相關的關係。

sections.heading: 學習流程
sections.body: 先讀出題幹中與「篇章」有關的條件；再以自己的話整理判斷依據；最後回到題目檢查結論。

sections.heading: 常見錯誤
sections.body: 不要只因看到「篇章」的名稱就作答；必須確認題幹證據與結論是否一致。

sections.heading: 自我檢核
sections.body: 嘗試在新情境中說明何時適用「篇章」，並指出至少一項支持判斷的條件。

studyHighlights: 先圈出與「篇章」直接相關的條件。
用自己的話說出判斷依據，不靠答案位置或關鍵字猜測。
回到原題檢查結論是否符合所有限制與資料。

body.heading: 從情境進入「篇章」
body.body: Imagine that your classmate posts: ‘I found a blue water bottle near the gym after lunch. Tell me where to return it.’ This is not merely a list of English sentences; it is a small text with a writer, a reader, a purpose, and a usable order of information. Read it once for the situation, then read it again to mark who, what, where, when, and what action is requested. Do not translate every word before forming a picture of the whole message. The first skill in this unit is to ask how each sentence helps the reader follow the same event.

body.heading: 建立「篇章」的概念架構
body.body: A coherent passage has more than correct grammar. Its sentences stay connected through a topic, a sensible sequence, reference words, and linking expressions. In ‘Mia missed the bus. She called her aunt because the rain became heavy,’ ‘She’ points back to Mia, while ‘because’ explains a reason. If a later sentence says ‘They’ without a clear possible referent, the reader must stop. A paragraph also has a communicative job: a notice gives essential action and time, a story develops events, and a dialogue reveals speakers’ responses. Learn to read both the language inside a sentence and the relationship between sentences.

body.heading: 用自編資料走完一次
body.body: Use this original text: ‘The art club will meet in Room 204 on Thursday at 4:10. Bring a pencil and the poster draft. If you cannot come, send your ideas to Leo before noon.’ First write the text’s purpose in one phrase: it is an invitation with preparation and an alternative action. Then connect each detail to a question—where, when, what to bring, and what to do if absent. The pronoun ‘you’ addresses the club members, and ‘If’ marks a condition. Notice that the final sentence is not an unrelated fact; it completes the notice by helping a different situation.

body.heading: 依步驟完成練習
body.body: Now work with four cards: ‘The library closes at five.’ ‘Please return the tablets.’ ‘So our science group must finish the survey early.’ ‘This rule starts today.’ Arrange them for a school notice, then explain your order rather than guessing from vocabulary. Add ‘therefore’ or ‘because’ only when the relationship is justified. Next replace ‘the tablets’ with a noun that makes the reference clear, and check whether ‘This rule’ still has an identifiable antecedent. A good revision changes one relation at a time: topic, reference, time, or reason.

body.heading: 換到新情境仍能使用
body.body: Take one event—the class will collect used books—and create two texts with different readers. For classmates, write a short message that names the date, place, and requested action. For the principal, write a more formal notice that explains the purpose and reports how the books will be used. The facts should remain consistent, but the greeting, tone, amount of context, and sentence order can change. Compare your versions: if a reader can act without asking a missing question, the passage is doing its job. If a claim comes from a picture or table, identify exactly which visible detail supports it.

body.heading: 回顧證據與限制
body.body: To close the lesson, return to the water-bottle message and label four layers: situation, key information, connections, and reader action. Explain one answer with a quotation or a precise paraphrase from the text; ‘it sounds right’ is not enough. Then test the passage by changing the time or audience and list the sentences that must change. A complete understanding of Ae means you can follow a text as a whole, trace what each pronoun or connector does, and revise a passage so that another reader can understand and respond without relying on your private guess.

summary: 能從主題、目的、讀者與資訊順序說明一段英文文本如何完成溝通。
能用主旨、細節、代名詞先行詞與連接詞指出篇章關係的證據。
能依文本類型和受眾改寫通知、訊息或對話，同時維持事實一致。
能在改變時間、人物或目的後找出必須調整的句子，並說明修正理由。

exitCheck.prompt: In the original art-club notice, how do the sentences work together to help a reader act?
exitCheck.expectedEvidence: 能指出文本目的、至少兩項細節，以及時間、條件或連接詞如何支援行動。

exitCheck.prompt: Why is a grammatically correct sentence not always a good part of a passage? Give an example involving reference or order.
exitCheck.expectedEvidence: 能以代名詞先行詞不清、連接關係錯誤或資訊順序不當的例子說明篇章連貫問題。

exitCheck.prompt: Rewrite the same event for a classmate and for the principal. What must stay the same, and what may change?
exitCheck.expectedEvidence: 能維持事件事實與必要資訊，並說明受眾改變時語氣、背景、稱呼或資訊順序的調整。
